layers.note: A wiry grass growing up through and beneath shrubs, where browsing cannot reach it.

moisture.note: Dry mesas, hills, canyons and rocky deserts (Hitchcock).

elevation_m.note: 230 to 1,300 m (FEIS), to 1,900 m in Colorado; 1,800 to 5,000 feet in Arizona (Kearney and Peebles).

shade_tolerance.note: FEIS: shade tolerant, surviving beneath mesquite canopies; now generally found growing under the protection of shrubs.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 2 to 15 °C; gone below −1 °C and above 18 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −15 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −20 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 25 to 34 °C; gone below 22 °C, where summers are too short, and above 36 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 4,600 to 10,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 3,800.

degree_days_5.note: About 3,000 to 8,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 2,200.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.06 to 0.35, gone by 0.03 and above 0.45.

summer_rain.note: Needs the monsoon's summer rain: from about 0.2 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone below 0.1; up to about 0.75, gone by 0.85.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Bush muhly grows from Colorado and Nevada to western Texas, Arizona, California and northern Mexico (FEIS; Kearney and Peebles). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
